requirements_summary: Silverpine requires: (1) clear latency SLO definitions (p50/p95/p99) for streaming and non-streaming paths; (2) telemetry that separates client-side end-to-end from server ingress->egress and kernel/token-level timings; (3) reserved GPU pool sizing for 1.2k concurrent shoppers, 5M tokens/day, burst capacity for flash sales; (4) SLA language with credits tied to p95 violations and documented measurement methodology; (5) support for VPC + KMS and EU data residency for order history embeddings.
latency_slo_details: Target non-streaming chat: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 220ms, p99 < 450ms (end-to-end client perceived)
Streaming chat: first-byte p50 < 50ms, first-byte p95 < 150ms; streaming tail p99 < 600ms for continuous token delivery
Tokenization/TTFB vs final response: want both first-token and completion times logged
Measurement zones: client-side (mobile/web), edge ingress->egress, server kernel/token pipeline — require correlation IDs
Prefer Redwood SDK to emit client timestamps + server receipts; cross-validate with synthetic probes from Silverpine infra
measurement_alignment_notes: Customer and Redwood to agree on canonical timing windows. Silverpine insists on client-side RUM-style numbers for product KPIs; Redwood proposes canonical server-side p95 for SLA. Proposed dual-reporting approach: canonical SLA uses server ingress->egress aggregated by request route, product metrics use client-side aggregated RUM. Need doc that defines: what counts as request (retries, timeouts), streaming chunk boundaries, partial-delivery success. Agreed to flush 48h test and compare both metrics.
reserved_capacity_plan: Initial reserve: equivalent of 8x 80GB A100 pods (steady), autoscale burst to 20x for 10-20 minute windows; expectation: 1.2k concurrent chat sessions, batching average 1.8x efficiency; Redwood to produce kernel-level latency profile and advised quantization (int8) to meet tail SLOs.
sla_negotiation_points: Primary items: define measurement endpoint, dispute window (10 business days), credit formula for p95 breaches, scheduled maintenance windows, rollback/fallback rules and costs for cross-region failover. Silverpine requests 99.95% availability + p95 latency target in SLA for first 6 months after go-live.
